bugs.title: Changing the country from المزيد freezes the page: main, top bar and bottom nav stay inert until reload
bugs.width: 390 (phones; desktop can escape with the Esc key)
bugs.evidence: Found by reading the code. The flow never hit it: country_switch_SA reloaded right after picking SA and never clicked anything. The production /assets/shell.8f7a80f4be.js is byte-identical to src/shell.js (diffed). Opening المزيد calls open(), which runs inert(true) on main, .top, .tabbar, .foot and .mini (shell.js:21,24). Tapping «بلدك · غيّر» (#more #ctry) goes through shell.js:43. That line hides the sheet by setting hidden=true, hides the scrim and removes 'locked', but it never calls inert(false) or closeAll(). The only inert(false) is inside closeAll (shell.js:22). app.js:24 then removes #ctrybox, runs applyCountry() and calls home(), and nothing restores the page. The result is that every link, the search icon and the bottom tab bar stop responding to taps. The tifoOv history entry pushed by open() is also left behind. The first back gesture only uses up that entry (popstate at shell.js:33 finds no open sheet), and the second one leaves the page. On a phone the only way out is a reload.
bugs.fix: At shell.js:43, close the sheet through closeAll('now'), which runs inert(false) and pops the tifoOv entry, before app.js opens #ctrybox. A simpler option is to make #ctrybox a real sheet opened with open(). Add #ctrybox to the popstate cleanup.
bugs.verified:
I could not refute this. The bug is confirmed from the production code, not only the source files. Production /assets/shell.8f7a80f4be.js is byte-identical to src/shell.js (cmp returned SAME). The live app.8f7a80f4be.js contains the same country-pick handler.

On the live homepage, #ctry sits inside the sheet div#more, which has role=dialog and starts hidden.

The flow step by step:
1. Opening المزيד calls open() (shell.js:24). That runs inert(true), which sets .inert on main, .top, .tabbar, .foot and .mini (shell.js:21), and pushes a history entry {tifoOv:1}.
2. Tapping #ctry hits the capture-phase handler at shell.js:43. It only sets sheet.hidden=true and scrim.hidden=true and removes the 'locked' class. It never calls inert(false) and never pops the history entry.
3. app.js:21-24 then appends #ctrybox to body. Body is not in the inert list, so the picker can still be tapped. Picking a country runs box.remove(), applyCountry() and home() (home page only).
4. The only inert(false) in the codebase is inside closeAll (shell.js:22), and nothing on this path calls it. main and the other four elements stay inert.

The reporter's side notes also hold:
- **Esc gets out:** the keydown handler at shell.js:47 calls closeAll(), and that always runs inert(false), even with no sheet open. That explains why desktop can escape with Esc.
- **Back needs two swipes:** popstate at shell.js:33 finds no open sheet, so the first back gesture only uses up the leftover tifoOv entry.

I did not reproduce it in a browser, because Chromium was not allowed. The existing captures in /root/.claude/jobs/abd28f85/tmp/qa never exercise this flow.
bugs.corrected: The report is accurate. The fix it proposes is sound: at shell.js:43, close the sheet with closeAll('now'), which runs inert(false) and pops the tifoOv history entry, before app.js appends #ctrybox. Alternatively, make #ctrybox a real sheet opened with open(). The same shell.js:43 branch also handles #srch, so search probably leaves the page inert the same way. That is only by analogy, though: #srch is not inside #more, and I did not verify that path.

ما في مواجهات سابقة مسجّلة.

bugs.title: Mini-bar share button wraps onto a second row and sits on the first match tab
bugs.evidence: flows/pick_before_reload.png and flows/pick_after_reload.png: once the page scrolls, the share icon (box with up-arrow) is drawn on top of the «قبل المباراة» tab label, under the mini-bar. .mini .wrap is grid-template-columns:1fr auto 1fr auto (4 tracks, block-size 3rem). On match pages miniDraw() puts 5 children in it: home, score, away, the cinema [data-cine] button and the share [data-sheet=share] button. The 5th child wraps into an implicit second row at the inline-start (right) edge, which overflows the 3rem bar onto the sticky .mtabs (top: calc(var(--topH)+3rem), or 3rem on phones). The share button now covers the first tab's tap target.
bugs.fix: Use grid-template-columns:1fr auto 1fr auto auto (or grid-auto-flow:column) for .mini .wrap, so the cinema and share buttons both stay on the one 3rem row.
bugs.verified: Confirmed on production. The live CSS at /assets/tifo.8f7a80f4be.css still has `.mini .wrap{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr auto 1fr auto;...;block-size:3rem}`. Nothing overrides it, and `.mini .ib{display:inline-grid}` does not hide either button. /m/6040358/ has `<body data-page="match">`, and in the live shell.js `PAGE = B.dataset.page`. So miniDraw() in src/shell.js:111 (same code on production) writes 5 children: .mt, .ms, .mt.a, button[data-cine] and button[data-sheet=share]. With only 4 tracks, the 5th child (share) goes into an implicit second row at the inline-start edge, which is the right edge in RTL. That row is outside the 3rem bar. On phones the bar sits at top 0 and `body.mini-on .mtabs{inset-block-start:3rem}`, so the second row lands on the tab strip. Both screenshots, /root/.claude/jobs/abd28f85/tmp/qa/flows/pick_before_reload.png and pick_after_reload.png, show the share icon (box with up-arrow) drawn on top of the «قبل المباراة» tab label at the far right, just under the mini-bar. The cinema icon sits correctly at the far left of the bar in the 4th track. Code, production assets and screenshots all agree.
bugs.corrected: The diagnosis is correct. One refinement to the fix: `1fr auto 1fr auto auto` would leave an empty 5th track plus an extra .6rem gap on non-match pages, where miniDraw only writes 4 children because there is no cinema button. A version that fits both cases: `.mini .wrap{grid-template-columns:1fr auto 1fr;grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:auto}`. The icon buttons then get their own auto columns on the one 3rem row whether there are one or two of them. Alternatively, put the two buttons in a single wrapper span so there are always 4 children.

bugs.title: Upcoming match pages stay 'stale': hero kickoff dimmed to 50% and a fixed «آخر تحديث 07:12 ص» chip
bugs.files: site/build.cjs:113 and :684 (near = kickoff within 36 h), site/src/app.js:71 and :237-239, site/src/shell.js:177-179, site/src/v3.css:510
bugs.evidence: match_6040358_390_first.png and match_6040358_1440_first.png: the hero «17:00» and the date are grey (html.stale → .stale .board .sc .dg{opacity:.5}, and the mini-bar .ms too), and a «آخر تحديث 07:12 ص» chip sits in the hero. The page's data-built is 2026-09-28T03:12:35Z and it was captured about an hour later. Compare /m/1000020530/, which is not 'near' and so has no data-built: its «17:15» is white. Only stamp() removes the stale class, and match() never calls it here, because /v1/match/6040358.json is 404 (the detail isn't built for upcoming matches) and the catch only retries within 90 min of kickoff. Every scheduled match 1.5-36 h out therefore looks broken for most of a day. The chip also uses 12-hour «ص» (shell.js:178 has no hourCycle:'h23'), while app.js:71 uses 24-hour.
bugs.fix: When the match JSON is 404 and the match is scheduled, treat it as fresh: stamp with live.json.generated or the build time, or don't give scheduled matches data-built. Add hourCycle:'h23' to the stale chip's time format.
bugs.verified:
I reproduced the bug on production and traced it in the code, so it is not refuted.

1. **Live checks (04:37Z):**
   - https://tifo.elyoxe.com/m/6040358/ has `data-built="2026-09-28T03:12:35.766Z"` and the inline script that adds `html.stale` once the page is more than 120 s old.
   - `/v1/match/6040358.json` returns 404.
   - `live.json` has no entry for this match.
   - Kickoff is Tuesday 29 Sep at 17:00 UAE, about 32 h away.

2. **Why the page gets `data-built`:** in `build.cjs:684`, `near` is true when kickoff is within ±36 h. So `liveish` at `build.cjs:112` is true, and the page is stamped and dimmed after 2 minutes.

3. **Why it never clears:** in `src/app.js`, `match()` fails when the match JSON is 404. Its catch only retries for matches that are live or within 90 min of kickoff. `stamp()` is the only thing that removes the `stale` class and fires `tifo:fresh`, and it is never reached. `overlay()` is only started after a successful load. The chip that `shell.js:177-179` adds is removed only on `tifo:fresh`, so it stays too.

4. **Screenshot:** `match_6040358_390_first.png` shows the dimmed «17:00» and date, and the «آخر تحديث 07:12 ص» chip.

5. **12-hour time:** `shell.js:178` has no `hourCycle`, while `app.js:71` uses `hourCycle:"h23"`. That produces the 12-hour «ص» in the chip.

The proposed fix is sound: treat a 404 on a scheduled match as fresh by stamping with `live.json.generated` or the build time, or don't give scheduled matches without a detail file `data-built`. Also add `hourCycle:'h23'` to the chip's time format.

bugs.title: Gulf Cup and Premier League both show the «البطولة متوقفة أو خلصت هالموسم» banner, but both competitions are still being played
bugs.files: site/build.cjs:419 (c.dormant note); poller.py:486 (dormant rule); poller.py:448 (dormant = daily refresh); /v1/index.json
bugs.evidence:
Both hero sections print «البطولة متوقفة أو خلصت هالموسم. هذي آخر نتايجها.» because /v1/index.json has dormant:true for 329 (Gulf Cup) and 47 (Premier League). Rule at poller.py:486: dormant only when no kickoff falls between 3 days ago and 30 days ahead.

The flags break that rule:
- /v1/comp/329/fixtures.json: group round 3 on 2026-09-29/30, semis on 10-03, final on 10-06, so the next match is tomorrow. Flag: true.
- /v1/comp/47/fixtures.json: round 6 on 2026-10-10, 12 days away. Flag: true.
- UAE 538: next match 2026-10-16, 18 days away. Flag: false.

The same hero shows «الجولة الياية 3 الثلاثاء 29 سبتمبر» (Gulf Cup) and «6 السبت 10 أكتوبر» (PL), so the page contradicts itself.

Effects at 390:
- Gulf Cup: the two group leaders fill hero slots 1–2, and v3.css `.chero .hfacts div:nth-child(n+3){display:none}` hides «الجولة الياية». A phone user sees only the stopped banner (c_gulf_cup_390_first.png).
- PL: the banner pushes the table down, so only 4 rows sit above the tab bar instead of the target 6 (c_premier_league_390_first.png).

Dormant also means a daily refresh (poller.py:448), which likely causes the stale Gulf Cup simulation in the next bug.
bugs.fix: Fix the poller state for 329 and 47 by recomputing dormant from the fixture list it keeps. The 47 note at poller.py:475 shows FotMob sent no fixtures at 04:00; check that the deployed Lambda has the fallback before the dormant calculation. As a guard in build.cjs, show the note only when fx has no kickoff within −3 to +30 days.
bugs.verified:
I confirmed the bug on production. I did not refute it. 1. **/v1/index.json (curl --compressed):** 329 gulf-cup shows `dormant:true, matches:0, finished:0, next_kickoff:null, updated 2026-09-28T00:00:31Z`. 47 premier-league shows `dormant:true, matches:0, next_kickoff:null, updated 00:00:33Z`. 538 shows `dormant:false, next_kickoff 2026-10-16T13:05Z`. 2. **Fixture files:** - /v1/comp/329/fixtures.json has kickoffs on 2026-09-29 and 09-30, and later rounds. - /v1/comp/47/fixtures.json has 380 matches, `generated` 2026-09-27T21:58:34Z, with kickoffs from 2026-10-10 onwards. That is inside the +30-day window, so under poller.py's rule (`dormant = not any(now-3d <= k <= now+30d)`) both should be false. 3. **Live pages:** both /c/gulf-cup/ and /c/premier-league/ contain «متوقفة» once, the note from build.cjs:419 `${c.dormant ? '

البطولة متوقفة أو خلصت هالموسم…' : ""}`. The same hero also prints «الجولة الياية 3 الثلاثاء 29 سبتمبر» and «6 السبت 10 أكتوبر», so each page contradicts itself as reported. The screenshots named in the report exist in the qa folder (c_gulf_cup_390_first.png and c_premier_league_390_first.png). 4. **Likely cause:** the 00:00 poller run got no matches for both competitions. index.json shows matches:0 at the same 00:00 timestamp. The dormant flag was then computed from an empty list. poller.py now has a fallback that keeps the last good fixture list when FotMob sends none, and it runs before the dormant calculation. So either that fallback was not deployed in the Lambda at 00:00, or it did not fire. The index row still shows matches:0 and next_kickoff:null, so it was not applied. 5. **Knock-on effect:** a dormant competition refreshes only every `heavy_dormant_minutes` (1440, i.e. daily), per comp_due_minutes. The stale state therefore persists. The proposed fix is sound: - Recompute dormant from the kept or last-good fixtures, and confirm the deployed build/lambda/poller.py carries the fallback. - Add a guard in build.cjs:419 that shows the note only when `fx.matches` has no kickoff between −3 and +30 days. - The same guard should apply at build.cjs:326, 327 and 468. Those lines also use `c.dormant`, which drops these competitions from the home competition grid and the "now" selection.

1. **Code:** v3.js wraps everything in `(function(root){...})(this)` (line 188). In Node, `this` at the top of a module is the original `module.exports` object. Line 180 then replaces `module.exports` with R, so that original object stays empty and `root.ARABT` is undefined at build time. `heroPick` (v3.js:112) reads `AT = (root && root.ARABT) || {}` and never looks at an `opts.arabT`. build.cjs:451 calls `R.heroPick(day.matches, index, null, null)` while it passes `{arabT:ARABT}` to `homeRails` on the same line. **About the proposed fix:** of the two options given, only adding `opts.arabT` to `heroPick` works as-is. Setting `R.ARABT` works only if `heroPick` also reads `R.ARABT`, because `root` inside v3.js is not reachable from build.cjs.

- The current build is dated 04:29:54Z, not 03:12Z; the wrong hero (6150377) is the same.
- For the fix, add an `opts.arabT` argument to `heroPick` (`var AT = (opts && opts.arabT) || (root && root.ARABT) || {}`) and pass `{arabT:ARABT}` at build.cjs:451. bugs.title: Service worker: a connection that fails after more than 4 s shows the browser error page, not /offline/
bugs.evidence: `slow = timeout(4000).then(()=>caches.match(req)).then(hit => hit || net)` takes on `net` when nothing is cached. When `net` then rejects, as it does on a weak stadium signal after a DNS or TCP timeout, `slow` rejects within a few microtasks. The race's other branch, `net.catch(()=>caches.match(...).then(...caches.match('/offline/')))`, is still waiting on two Cache Storage reads. Promise.race therefore rejects, respondWith gets a rejected promise, and Chrome shows its own 'No internet' page. The /offline/ fallback only works when the network fails immediately, which is the case QA tested (offlineNav PASS).
bugs.fix: Make the slow branch fall back itself: `.then(hit => hit || net.catch(fallback))`, with one shared fallback function. Or have `slow` never reject, for example `hit || new Promise(()=>{})`.
bugs.verified:
I fetched the production https://tifo.elyoxe.com/sw.js (V=8f7a80f4be) and compared it with /root/workspace/saas/football/site/src/sw.js. Line 49 and the lines around it match. The non-live fetch handler covers navigations such as /laws/ and /v1 data outside LIVE:

  const slow = new Promise(ok => setTimeout(ok, 4000)).then(() => caches.match(e.request)).then(hit => hit || net);
  return Promise.race([net.catch(() => caches.match(e.request).then(hit => { ... return caches.match("/offline/")... })), slow]);

Working through the promises confirms the report. Take a page that is not in tifo-pages, where `net` (the preloadResponse or fetch) rejects after the 4 s timer.

1. At 4 s, `slow` has already resolved its callback to the pending `net` promise, so `slow` follows `net`'s state.
2. When `net` rejects, `slow` rejects within about 2 microtasks.
3. The catch branch has to wait on two Cache Storage reads first: caches.match(req), then caches.match('/offline/'). These are real I/O and finish on later tasks, not microtasks.
4. Promise.race settles on `slow`'s rejection first. respondWith gets a rejected promise, and Chrome shows its own network error page instead of /offline/.

Timing decides which case works:
- If `net` fails before 4 s, the catch branch settles long before the timer, and /offline/ is served. That is the case QA tested (offlineNav PASS).
- If the page is cached, `slow` returns the cached hit at 4 s, which is fine.
- Only the path with no cache and a failure after 4 s breaks. A DNS or TCP timeout on a weak connection, or a preloadResponse that rejects late, produces it.

The same race also rejects plain /v1 data requests outside LIVE, but those have no /offline/ fallback anyway. The proposed fix is sound. Either make `slow` use `hit || net.catch(fallback)` with one shared fallback function, or make `slow` never reject.

I made no edits and launched no browser.
bugs.corrected: The bug is confirmed as reported. On a page with nothing cached, when the network fails after the 4 s budget, the `slow` branch follows `net`'s rejection. The page is «liveish», so the head script adds .stale once the build is more than 2 minutes old. app.js:232 clears it only after Promise.all([index(), get("match/"+ID+".json")]) succeeds, but /v1/match/6040358.json returns 404 (the capture's failed requests list it). So stamp() never runs and .stale never clears.

In match_6040358_390_first.png the 17:00 kick-off, the date and the countdown are at opacity .5 (v3.css:510). A pill reads «آخر تحديث 07:12 ص»: shell.js:178 formats the time without hourCycle:"h23", so it uses a 12-hour clock with «ص», while the footer uses 24-hour time. /m/1000020530/ has no data-built attribute and renders normally.
bugs.fix: For status==='scheduled', stamp with the index/day payload when the detail JSON is 404, or skip the stale marking for scheduled matches more than 2 h away. Add hourCycle:'h23' to the stale-pill time format.
bugs.verified:
Confirmed on production. Evidence:
(1) curl https://tifo.elyoxe.com/v1/match/6040358.json returns HTTP 404.
(2) The live /m/6040358/ HTML carries data-built="2026-09-28T04:29:54.532Z" and the inline head script that adds html.stale once the build is more than 120 s old. The match is status "scheduled", kickoff 2026-09-29T13:00Z, so the page is liveish.
(3) The deployed app.8f7a80f4be.js matches src/app.js:232. match() runs Promise.all([index(), get("match/"+ID+".json")]), and stamp(), the only thing that removes .stale and fires tifo:fresh (app.js:71), is called only on success. Its .catch retries only when MD is set and the match is live or within 90 min of kickoff, so with a 404 nothing ever clears .stale. overlay() also calls stamp(), but overlay() is only started after a successful match(), so it never runs either.
(4) v3.css:510 dims .stale .kick to opacity .5.
(5) The deployed shell.8f7a80f4be.js line 178 formats the stale pill with toLocaleTimeString("ar-AE-u-nu-latn", {hour:"2-digit", minute:"2-digit", timeZone:"Asia/Dubai"}) and no hourCycle:"h23". stamp() in app.js:71 does pass h23, so the two formats don't match.
(6) The screenshot match_6040358_390_first.png shows the dimmed 17:00, the dimmed date and the countdown, plus a pill reading «آخر تحديث 07:12 ص».
One small point: the built timestamp in production is now 04:29Z (08:29 Dubai), so the capture came from an earlier build, but the mechanism is the same.
bugs.corrected: Bug confirmed as reported. When a near-term scheduled match has no /v1/match/{id}.json (404), .stale never clears. Stamp from the index/day data when the detail file is 404, or skip the head stale script for scheduled matches. Also add hourCycle:"h23" to shell.js:178.

bugs.fix: Use ${r.gd > 0 ? "+" + r.gd : r.gd}, matching render.js:135.
bugs.verified: I checked the code, the live page and the screenshot, and all three confirm the bug. In build.cjs:636 the stakes row writes goal difference as `${r.gd > 0 ? "+" + r.gd : r.gd}`, with no and no LTR isolation. The live HTML at /m/1000020530/ serves bare `-1` cells inside the `#stakes` section. bugs.fix: Write an empty {"players":[]} birthdays file for every day. Don't fetch match detail for far fixtures (see the first finding). Publish /favicon.ico, or add <link rel=icon href=/favicon.svg> in ehead().
bugs.verified:
I checked with curl --compressed on 2026-09-28, in the code under /root/workspace/saas/football/site, and in the capture logs under /root/.claude/jobs/abd28f85/tmp/qa (manifest.json, flows.json).
- /v1/players/birthdays/09-28.json returns 404 (text/html, 2811 B). src/app.js:473 always fetches "players/birthdays/"+md+".json" and uses .catch(draw) to swallow the failure, but the browser still logs the failed request. flows.json shows "404 /v1/players/birthdays/09-28.json" 24 times, and manifest.json notes that 09-27 and 09-28 are 404 while 09-29 is 200.
- /v1/match/1000020530.json and /v1/match/6040358.json both return 404. The match page fetch at src/app.js:232 runs even for far fixtures. manifest.json records this as detail files not built until 48 h / 75 min before kickoff.
- /favicon.ico returns 404 (2811 B of HTML). /favicon.svg returns 200. The home page has <link rel="icon" href="/favicon.svg">. The ehead() output at build.cjs:868, which is /embed/t/?c=538 on production, has no icon link, so the browser asks for /favicon.ico there.

- manifest.json shows 26 "Failed to load resource ... 404" console lines.
The bug is confirmed. It is low severity: noise and wasted requests, nothing breaks.
bugs.corrected: The bug is real, but some wording needs correcting. The birthdays 404 happens only on days with no birthday file (09-27 and 09-28 are 404, 09-29 is 200), so it is not every home load. The /favicon.ico 404 comes only from the embed pages (ehead() in build.cjs:868), because normal pages already carry <link rel=icon href=/favicon.svg>. Some of the 26 console 404s come from missing logos that the report doesn't mention: /logo/-1.png, /logo/96/-1.webp for team id -1, and /logo/101700.png, /logo/96/101700.webp. Proposed fix: add <link rel=icon href=/favicon.svg> to ehead(); on the home page, publish an empty birthdays file each day or add a no-birthday flag to an index the home page already loads; skip the match-detail fetch when kickoff is more than 48 h away; skip the logo request when the team id is -1.

bugs.title: Pre-match page shows two different Maghrib times (18:14 twice, 18:09 once)
bugs.evidence: At 390 the page says «المغرب في أبوظبي 18:14 · بين الشوطين» in the hero and again at the top of «قبل المباراة» (shell.js). The details card adds a third mention, «أذان المغرب 18:09 يصادف الاستراحة، تقريبي» (render.js:263), which is computed for the stadium in Sharjah and doesn't name a city (match_upcoming_stakes_390_full.png). The reader gets two contradictory times for the same prayer, against rule 7 (a single place per piece of copy).
bugs.fix: Keep the visitor-city line only once (hero, or the pane before kickoff) and drop the build-time prayer tile. Or label the tile «في استاد الشارقة» and show it only when no client line is rendered.
bugs.verified: Confirmed on production and in the code. The live HTML for /m/1000020530/ contains the build-time tile `أذان المغرب 18:09يصادف الاستراحة، تقريبي`, which src/render.js:261-264 builds from md.prayer.clashes. The embedded data holds prayer.method "uae-awqaf-18.2", times_uae.maghrib "18:09" and the clash at_uae "18:09", segment "halftime", and it computes this for the venue (استاد الشارقة). The tile never names a city. The client line comes from src/shell.js prayLine (around lines 215-226). It falls back to the first city in the country list (Abu Dhabi for AE) and adds the Awqaf +4 min offset to maghrib, which gives «المغرب في أبوظبي 18:14 · بين الشوطين». The IIFE writes that line into the hero (#prayl, or a p.prayl before .hero-acts) and again after #wwbox when status==="scheduled", so it shows twice. Screenshot /root/.claude/jobs/abd28f85/tmp/qa/match_upcoming_stakes_390_full.png shows «المغرب في أبوظبي 18:14 · بين الشوطين» under the hero and again inside «وين تنقل», plus the «أذان المغرب 18:09 … تقريبي» tile in تفاصيل المباراة. The two times really differ: Sharjah is east of Abu Dhabi, so sunset comes about 5 min earlier. The page gives one prayer two unlabeled times, as reported.
bugs.corrected: The bug is confirmed as written. The 18:09 tile is computed server-side for the Sharjah venue (md.prayer, Awqaf method) and names no city. The 18:14 line is computed client-side for the visitor's city (Abu Dhabi by default) and is inserted twice, in the hero and after #wwbox. Fix: when prayLine renders, hide or remove the .tile.pray, or label the tile «في استاد الشارقة». Also stop inserting the second p.prayl.in after #wwbox (the 390 duplicate).

bugs.title: /arabs/ hub card links are about 22 px tall, well under a 44 px tap target
bugs.evidence: .agl{display:grid;gap:.25rem;font-size:.85rem} .agl a{…} gives inline text links about 22 px high on a 28 px pitch: «العرب في أوروبا / الحذاء الذهبي / أحسن لاعب عربي» sit at y≈449/477/505 in arabs_390_full.png. There are 12 such links across the four hub cards, stacked tightly enough that mis-taps are likely on a phone.
bugs.fix: .agl a{display:block;min-block-size:44px;padding-block:.6rem} (or display:flex;align-items:center), with gap:0.
bugs.verified: Live /arabs/ markup (curl --compressed): the hub cards use div.agl holding bare <a> links (for example العرب في أوروبا / الحذاء الذهبي / أحسن لاعب عربي, then المنتخبات العربية / فترة المنتخبات / مواجهات المنتخبات / العرب في كأس العالم, then the derbies card, then الانتقالات / الروزنامة / أرشيف النتايج). Source is /root/workspace/saas/football/site/src/v3.css:662: `.agl{display:grid;gap:.25rem;font-size:.85rem}.agl a{color:var(--ink);text-decoration:underline;...}`. Nothing sets padding, min-height or its own line-height on the links, so each one is only as tall as one line of 13.6px text, about 20 to 22px. I cropped /root/.claude/jobs/abd28f85/tmp/qa/arabs_390_full.png (390 px wide, so 1 image px = 1 CSS px) at y 380 to 560. The links sit on a pitch of about 28px, which matches the reported y≈449/477/505. Each is a single short text line with no padding. The reported claim holds.
bugs.corrected: Confirmed, but it is a low-priority, AAA-level issue. The targets are about 22px tall on a 28px pitch, well under the 44px of WCAG 2.5.5 (AAA) and Apple's HIG. They probably still pass WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8: that rule's spacing exception needs a 24px circle around each target, and 28px between centres leaves room. On a phone, though, each tap area is only about 22px. The proposed fix is sound: `.agl{gap:0} .agl a{display:flex;align-items:center;min-block-size:44px}` in src/v3.css:662. Each card has 3 or 4 links, so the cards will grow by about 60 to 90px each. Check the 880 and 1440 layouts after the change.
